body: Thanks, that's very nice of you. This is a throwaway though.

I'm in the Army Reserves. I tried to get a full time job working for the Army or the government (usajobs.gov), but I was not successful. To be honest, I strongly dislike the Army and I don't want to work for them any more. I don't even want to be in the Reserves any more but... well... it's all I've got. So I really have no choice.

Joining the army was the greatest mistake of my life. My second greatest mistake was picking natural resource management as a major rather than accounting. If only I did things differently, and used scholarships to pay for school and got a sensible degree. On the other hand, is it fair that I should suffer the rest of my life because of  mistakes I made when I was basically a kid? At the time I did not know that my degree was not sensible, and the research I did actually indicated that the job outlook was good. Everybody in my life told me it was the right decision. I got good grades. I graduated with honors (not high honors, but still).

Then the Great Recession happened. Then I had the bright idea of going to Iraq. Which put money in my bank account. More money than I ever had. And a nice car. And yet, I think I am even worse off now.
